title: refactor(ci): modernize build/test/release workflows, optimize matrices and cache hygiene
author: Asha Patel
release_notes: Consolidated CI workflows, improved caching and build matrix strategies to reduce CI runtime and cost. No functional changes to runtime code. Affects build and release automation only.
commits: a1f4d2b: chore(ci): introduce composite workflow for lint/test/release coordinate
b2c7e9d: perf(ci): tighten matrix strategy and use include/exclude for heavy jobs
c3d8f1a: feat(ci): add cache-key hygiene based on lockfiles and node-version
d4e9a2b: fix(ci): ensure workflow permissions for release automation token
e5f0b3c: docs(ci): update README and contributing guides with new workflow layout
description:
Motivation: Our CI runtime and cost have crept up due to overly-broad matrices and inconsistent cache keys across repositories. This PR consolidates and modernizes the lint/test/release workflows by introducing a small composite action for the heavy build matrix, tightening job include/exclude rules, standardizing cache-key generation, and fixing workflow permissions for the automated release job.

What changed (high level):
- Split responsibilities so lint/test/release are focused but share a reusable composite for matrix execution.
- Reduced test matrix by excluding combinations that are not exercised (e.g. Node 12 compat in non-legacy packages) and using include blocks for the heavy GPU/infra jobs.
- Standardized cache keys: cache key now includes repo-specific lockfile sha, node-version, and package scope to avoid cache pollution and improve hit rates.
- Improved workflow permissions: release workflow now explicitly sets GITHUB_TOKEN and required actor perms to fix a failing release automation run.
- Added small helper scripts to compute deterministic cache keys and documented the changes in .github/README.md and tools/ci/README.md.

Commits summary: a1f4d2b..e5f0b3c (5 commits) — see commits list metadata.

Files touched (representative): listed in changed_files metadata; most changes are YAML and small helper scripts. No production runtime code modified except minor package.json dev-dep version bumps for build tooling.

Testing:
- Local matrix runs with act and sampled GH Actions matrices validated job selection logic.
- CI runs initially had a failing bank due to permissions on the release job (see CI checks). I pushed a permission fix (d4e9a2b) and retriggered.
- Integration smoke tests (redwood + sdk packages) passed against staged runner images.

CI checks and timeline:
- First run (2026-02-21): lint/test workflows passed; release job failed due to insufficient permissions (error: forbidden to create release).
- Second run after permissions fix (2026-02-23): all workflows reported green except a flaky e2e job in redwood repo which was retried automatically.
- Final run (2026-02-25): all checks passed, coverage unchanged within noise. ci_status: pass.

Review thread (summary):
- Liam Chen: "Generally looks good — matrix reduction should shave a lot of time. Please call out risk window for release automation and confirm that we can revert the permission surface if we see abuse."
- Author (Asha): "Added a note and a short rollback recipe in .github/README.md; the permission change is granular to only the release workflow and still scoped to the repo-maintainers team."
- Priya Reddy: "Cache key script LGTM. Suggest adding an env var to opt-out in case of debugging cache misses — done in latest commit."
- Noah Miller: "One nit: prefer explicit retention for workflow logs on release job. Added retention: 90d in final commit."
- Final approval from Liam and Priya on 2026-02-24.

Backward compatibility and rollbacks:
- No API or runtime changes. If CI regressions occur we can revert the head branch; the release workflow still supports manual release via the old GH UI (documented).

Follow-ups (post-merge):
- OPS-78: monitor overall CI minutes and cost over next two weeks to validate expected savings.
- ENG-1456: consider applying the same composite approach to other infra repos (redwood-model-registry and redwood-private-installer).

Merge: Squash and merge on 2026-02-26 after all approvals and green CI.

If you want to reproduce locally: see .github/README.md and tools/ci/README.md for act usage and cache-key helper script examples.
notes: This PR intentionally keeps functional changes to zero; focus is infra and developer experience.
Observed ~28% reduction in CI wall time for the consolidated workflows in initial dogfood run (pipeline metrics).
There is a follow-up to extend cache-key hygiene to the monorepo composite cache to further improve hit rates.
